steps: Written first in tests/unit/notify.test.mjs: `buildEvent` with `kind=memory` and `memory=<path to a JSON file>` prints exactly the 14 keys of tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v2-memory.json in that order with `v` 2 and the file's object under `memory`; for each of the ten kinds of `KINDS` other than `memory` the output has the 13 keys of tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v1.json in order with `v` 1 and the same bytes as before this change (the existing test `buildEvent's keys are the v1 fixture's, in order` is extended to say so under a new name; its old name leaves tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt in the same commit); `memory=` with a v1 kind, and `kind=memory` without `memory=`, exit 2 and print nothing on stdout (`memory= is the memory kind's` on stderr for the first); `ROUTED` is `["park","needs_michael","blocked","debrief"]` unchanged and `ROUTED_V2` is it plus `memory`.

Written first in tests/unit/memreview.test.mjs: `card(v, m, items, policy)` from a verdicts object with one failed op gives `{pr, rules_pr, policy, reviewed, held, failed, failures, state, review}` with `failures[0]` `{id, section, q, reason}` (the `section` from the input item of that id, `q` 2, the `reason` without its ` (q2)` suffix), `state` `open` when `merged_by` is null and `merged` when it is `driver`; from a review none (no verdicts, `review` the why) `failures` is `[]` and `review` the why; `title(m)` prints `[<run>] memory: <held> held · <failed> failed` and `[<run>] memory: review none` when `review` is not `ok`; `node lib/memreview.mjs card <verdicts.json> <memory.json> <input.json> <policy>` prints the object as one JSON line.

features.description: At the end of memory_pr a run with a memory PR sends one `memory` notification: POSTed to EVENT_URL as the v2 event (no context bundle) when EVENT_URL and EVENT_V2=1 are both set, else the ntfy line with the title, the `memory:` line and both PRs as actions; a run with no PR sends none; the run's end notification and every v1 event keep their bytes.
steps: Written first, a new slow check file tests/checks/memory-event.sh (`# tier: slow` on line 2; its runs as tests/checks/memory-review.sh's `run` helper makes them, the stub curl recording each POST as tests/checks/event-run.sh reads it): `STUB_CURATOR_OPS=evict-two STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=evict-fails` under MEMORY_POLICY=pr with `EVENT_URL` and `EVENT_V2=1` in the user config → exactly one POST to EVENT_URL whose body is one JSON object with `v` 2, 14 keys, `kind` `memory`, `memory.failures[0].id` matching `^facts/[0-9]+$`, `memory.state` `open`, `memory.review` `ok`, and `body` equal to the run's `memory:` line in harness-log.md; no ntfy post whose Title is that event's title; `event → n8n: memory <id>` in the state's run.log after the line holding the `memory:` note; `events/<id>/event.json` under the state root and the record's memory-event.json both equal to the POSTed body; the run's end notification (the ntfy post titled with the run's end, normalised as event-run.sh's `nrec` does) byte-identical to the same stub run's with EVENT_URL and EVENT_V2 unset.

Written first in the same file: the same run with `EVENT_URL` set and `EVENT_V2` unset → no POST whose body has `"kind":"memory"`, one ntfy post whose Title is `[<run>] memory: 1 held · 1 failed`, whose body is the `memory:` line and whose Actions header names both PRs, and no `event hook failed` line in harness-log.md; with both unset → the same ntfy post; with both set and the stub curl answering 422 (a new fixture tests/fixtures/curl-event-422.out, the bytes real curl's `-w '%{http_code}'` prints, made as curl-event-500.out was, selected by `STUB_EVENT=422`) → the POST, then the ntfy post and the one note `event hook failed (422): memory; sent to ntfy`; `STUB_CURATOR_OPS=three-ops STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=hold` under MEMORY_POLICY=auto with both set → `memory.state` `merged` in the POSTed event and its run.log line after the merge note's; `STUB_CURATOR_OPS=proposal` under pr → no POST and no ntfy post titled `memory:` and no memory-event.json in the record; `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=none` on `fact-a` under pr → one event titled `[<run>] memory: review none` with `memory.failures` `[]` and `memory.review` the why; the first run's `events/<id>/event.json` with its id, `at` and URLs replaced by the placeholders equals tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v2-memory.json byte for byte (`cmp`), so the fixture n8n-home copies cannot drift from the driver's output.

lib/notify.sh: `notify`'s routing line routes `ROUTED`'s kinds when EVENT_URL is set and `memory` only when EVENT_URL and `EVENT_V2` are `1`, every other case to ntfy or NOTIFY_CMD with no POST and no note; `notify_event` skips the context bundle for `memory` (`context` null) and still writes `events/<id>/event.json`; lib/record.sh `memory_pr`: after the `memreview.mjs line` note, when `url` or `rurl` starts with `http`, `memreview.mjs card` writes `$SCRATCH/memory-event.json`, it is kept in the record as memory-event.json, and one `notify "$line" title=… body="$line" click=<facts PR else rules PR> actions=<both PRs via notify.mjs actions> kind=memory memory=$SCRATCH/memory-event.json priority=""` call follows; nothing is written or sent without a PR; lib/config.sh gains `EVENT_V2=""` beside EVENT_URL and templates/user/config.sh one commented `EVENT_V2=1` line under its EVENT_URL line; `bash -n lib/notify.sh lib/record.sh lib/config.sh tests/checks/memory-event.sh tests/stub-curl.sh` passes; `grep -n 'memory' lib/notify.sh` shows the routing line testing both `EVENT_URL` and `EVENT_V2`.

tests/checks/event-hook.sh and tests/checks/event-run.sh pass with no edit to any assertion (`git diff origin/main --stat -- tests/checks/event-hook.sh tests/checks/event-run.sh` prints nothing); `bash tests/run.sh event-hook event-run memory-event memory-review` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); memory-event.sh is timed once alone with `TEST_JOBS=4 bash tests/run.sh memory-event` and its row (file, tier slow, the seconds, the reason) is added under the table in journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md.

docs/architecture.md: `lib/notify.sh`'s row (the `EVENT_V2` rule, no bundle for `memory`), the CURATOR step's EVENT line, the config table's `EVENT_V2` row, the guards table's *Event hook fallback* row naming the `memory` kind; README.md's *Notifications* names the `memory` kind and `EVENT_V2`, its *Memory reviewer* the card; journal/decisions/2026-11-10-review-surface-event.md gains V1-02's rows marked *default* (one event per segment that reached a PR, each with its own id; no bundle; `EVENT_V2` as the switch) and the rejected list (probing the intake, a per-kind list in config, the silent 422 fallback, a bundle for the memory event).

The new check names are in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt (LC_ALL=C sorted) and no new name is in check-names-fast.txt (the file is slow); the entry's `checks` field counts V1's added, replaced and removed names against the budget of 15, with the reason when over.

features.description: An Opus review of V1's whole diff against the spec's four invariants, its Critical and Important findings fixed test-first, simplifications applied, the docs level; the review's file is docs/plans/2026-11-10-V1-review.md.
steps: `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- lib bin tests templates docs README.md journal/decisions > /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-11-10/V1.diff`; an Opus subagent reads the diff from that file (never the conversation) and writes docs/plans/2026-11-10-V1-review.md with findings graded Critical, Important, Minor, on at least: no v1 event changed a byte (`buildEvent` on each of the ten v1 kinds against tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v1.json, and tests/checks/event-hook.sh and event-run.sh unedited); `memory` is never POSTed with `EVENT_V2` unset whatever EVENT_URL says (`grep -n 'ROUTED\|EVENT_V2' lib/notify.sh lib/notify.mjs` and the routing line read); the end notification's bytes did not move (`finish` in lib/driver.sh is not in the diff, and memory-event.sh's byte compare); tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v2-memory.json is a run's output with placeholders, not typed (the fixture check in memory-event.sh); memory-event.json is written only when a PR exists (the `http` guard in lib/record.sh read). A second round only when the first found something Critical.

Every Critical and Important finding is fixed with a failing check or unit test first (names into tests/fixtures/check-names.txt, and check-names-fast.txt for unit names; a replaced check's old name leaves in the same commit); Minor findings are fixed or listed in the review file with why not; simplification passes the reviewer names are applied.

docs/architecture.md and README.md are read against the code as it stands (the `lib/notify.mjs`, `lib/notify.sh`, `lib/memreview.mjs` rows, the *Routed events* row, the config table, *Notifications*) and brought level; journal/decisions/2026-11-10-review-surface-event.md holds every V1 default marked *default* and lists V1's replaced and removed check names each with its successor, and the milestone's count against the budget of 15.

`bash -n` on every shell file the fixes touched and `node --check` on every .mjs pass; `bash tests/run.sh memory-event event-hook event-run` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: `lib/requests.mjs` judges a v2 request (`merge` or `close` on a PR of ledger/memory.jsonl, `why` within the hand decline's bounds) and prints the twelve-key v2 result and a `pr=` log line, and `harness memory decline <run> --why` writes the run-level declined row the next curator reads under *Michael declined*.
steps: Written first in tests/unit/requests.test.mjs: `validateRequest` with `--memory`'s rows (a facts row and a rules row of run `r1`, their `url`s) takes a v2 `merge` and a v2 `close` on a known PR of the right run as ok with `pr` (and `why` for the close) and no `text`; rejects `v` 2 with `answer` (`v 2 carries merge or close`), `v` 1 with `merge` (`verb is not answer or continue`), `v` 3 (`v is not 1 or 2`), a `pr` no row has (`pr <url> is not a memory PR the ledger knows (ledger/memory.jsonl)`), a `pr` of another run (`pr <url> belongs to run <row's run>, not <request's run>`), a `why` of two lines or 301 characters (`why must be one line of at most 300 characters`) and a `why` on a merge (`a merge takes no why`), the reason never holding the why's text; a v2 request still passes the id rule, the NUL rule, the 10 s grace and the duplicate rule; the existing test `v 2 is rejected` becomes `v 2 with answer is rejected, v 3 is not 1 or 2` (the old name leaves tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt in the same commit); `resultJson` for a v2 request has the twelve keys `v,id,at,verb,run,ok,exit,output,runner_started,refused,pr,state` in order with `v` 2 and `runner_started` false, and a v1 result keeps its ten; `logLine` carries `pr=<url>` after `run=` for a v2 request and never a why; the `validate` CLI takes `--memory <file>` and prints `pr` and `why` as labelled lines (the why to `--out`'s directory as `text` is, never on stdout).

Written first in tests/unit/memory.test.mjs: `answerRow` with no `n` gives `{run, project, n: null, tier: 1, verdict: "declined", why, file: null, section: null, text: null, key: null, at}` and `upsert` replaces an earlier run-level row of the same run and leaves its numbered rows; `memory.mjs main answer` for `<run>` without `/<n>` writes that row; in tests/unit/curator.test.mjs: `answersText` renders a run-level declined row as `- the facts PR of <run>, closed: <why>` under *Michael declined*, and `apply` with a run-level declined row in `--answers` drops no op (a null key matches nothing); in tests/unit/summary.test.mjs: `memoryOverride` reads a closed facts PR of a run whose only declined row is run-level as no override, extending the existing override test under a new name (the old name leaves both fixtures in the same commit); `proposalsView` and `answersTally` count the run-level row as one declined answer of its run.

Written first, a new fast check file tests/checks/memory-requests.sh (`# tier: fast` on line 2; no stub run: a ledger built from tests/fixtures/memory's result files as tests/checks/request-files.sh builds its state, `HARNESS_GH` tests/stub-gh.sh, `HARNESS_NOW` the fake clock): `harness memory decline <run> --why "<text>"` by hand appends one run-level row to the ledger's memory-answers.jsonl and makes one ledger commit (`git -C <ledger> log --oneline` grows by one line), and `harness memory decline <run>` without `--why` prints one `usage:` line on stderr and exits 1 with no row written.

lib/requests.mjs: `validateRequest`'s v2 branch after the v1 rules it shares (the id, the run pattern, the real run, no NUL, the grace), `--memory <file>` read in node, `resultJson`'s `pr` and `state`, `logLine`'s `pr=`; lib/memory.sh: `decline <run> --why` beside `decline <run>/<n> --why` with the usage line saying so, and bin/harness's usage line for `harness memory decline <run> --why`; lib/memory.mjs: `answerRow` without `n`, `upsert`'s key; lib/curator.mjs: `answersText`'s run-level line and `apply`'s null-key guard if one is needed; `node --check lib/requests.mjs lib/memory.mjs lib/curator.mjs` and `bash -n lib/memory.sh bin/harness tests/checks/memory-requests.sh` pass.

tests/fixtures/requests/merge.json, close.json and close-why.json each hold one v2 request with the keys `v,id,at,verb,run,pr[,why],source,event` in that order, written by one node command recorded in tests/fixtures/requests/README.md (`JSON.stringify(request) + "\n"` in one write, as the README's make.mjs wrote the v1 three) and a unit test in tests/unit/requests.test.mjs says each file is that command's bytes; tests/fixtures/requests/result-v2.json is the stdout of `node lib/requests.mjs result` for a v2 merge, copied from the unit test's run; README.md in that directory lists the four files with their ids and values.

docs/architecture.md's `lib/requests.mjs` row names the v2 verbs, `--memory`, the twelve-key result and `pr=`, its *Request inbox* state row names v2, and its `harness memory` row names `decline <run> --why`; README.md's `harness memory accept|decline` row names the run-level form; journal/decisions/2026-11-10-review-surface-verbs.md is created (title, provenance, finding · choice · rejected) with V2-01's rows marked *default* (one shape per version; a why refused on a merge; the run-level row's shape) and the rejected list so far.

The new names are in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt, both LC_ALL=C sorted; `node --test --test-isolation=none tests/unit/requests.test.mjs tests/unit/memory.test.mjs tests/unit/curator.test.mjs tests/unit/summary.test.mjs` passes every test; `bash tests/run.sh memory-requests request-files` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).

features.description: `harness requests` runs a v2 `merge` or `close`: gh's state first, the review rule, then `gh pr merge <url> --merge` or `gh pr close <url> [--comment <why>]` as argv, a close with a why writing the decline rows (run-level for the facts PR, one per `rules/<n>` for the rules PR), its refusals in the result and `pr=` in requests.log, `merged_by` left null so `harness memory` counts the merge as Michael's.
steps: Written first in tests/checks/memory-requests.sh (requests made from tests/fixtures/requests/merge.json, close.json and close-why.json with jq as request-files.sh's `req` does; the facts and rules PRs made in the stub gh so `pr-N` files exist): a `merge` of the facts PR touches `pr-N.merged` in the stub, its result in `requests/done/<id>.json` has `ok` true, `state` `merged`, `v` 2 and the twelve keys in order, and `requests.log`'s line holds `pr=<url>` and no why; a `merge` of the rules PR merges it the same way and `harness memory` then prints `merged unchanged` for both rows with no `override:`; a second `merge` of a merged PR (a new id) is refused `pr <url> is already merged` and moves to `requests/rejected/`; a `close` without a why touches `pr-N.closed`, writes no memory-answers.jsonl row, and `harness memory` prints `closed against a hold` for a row whose every op held; a `close` of the facts PR with a why touches `pr-N.closed`, keeps the why as `pr-N.comment`, writes one run-level declined row and `harness memory` prints no `override:` for that row; a `close` of the rules PR with a why writes one declined row per `rules/<n>` of the run's memory-result.json and `harness memory proposals <run>` shows each verdict; a `merge` of a PR whose row's `review` is not `ok` is refused `the review did not run for <url> (<why>): merge it on GitHub if you mean to` and no `pr-N.merged` appears; a `pr` no row has and a `pr` of another run are refused with V2-01's reasons; a second request with the first's id stands on the first result (one `done/<id>.json`, unchanged); with `STUB_REFUSE_MERGE=1` the result is `ok` false with gh's GraphQL line in `output` and `refused` null, nothing in `rejected/`; a `why` holding a backtick, `$(` and a quote reaches `pr-N.comment` byte for byte and `grep -c 'eval\|bash -c' lib/requests.sh` prints 0.

tests/stub-gh.sh: `pr merge <url> --merge` without `--match-head-commit` merges the head branch's tip into the bare origin's main and touches `pr-N.merged` (the `STUB_REFUSE_MERGE` line kept); `pr close <url> [--comment <text>]` by URL touches `pr-N.closed` and writes the comment to `pr-N.comment`, each line copied from gh 2.45's behaviour as the `pr view --json commits` shape was, named in the stub's header comment; `bash -n tests/stub-gh.sh` passes and `bash tests/run.sh memory-review memory-branch lanes-record-pr` still ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).

lib/requests.sh `one()`: the v2 branch after the claim reads `pr`, `why` and the row's `review` from `validate`'s labelled lines, runs `$GH pr view <url> --json state` first (`MERGED` and `CLOSED` refused as V2-01 names them, an unreadable answer `ok` false with gh's text), refuses a `merge` whose row's `review` is not `ok`, then runs `gh pr merge <url> --merge` or `gh pr close <url>` plus `--comment "$why"` as argv elements only, writes `state` `merged` or `closed` into the result through `requests.mjs result --pr --state`, and after a close with a why calls `harness memory decline <run>/<n> --why` per `rules/<n>` of the ledger's memory-result.json for the rules PR or `harness memory decline <run> --why` for the facts PR, a failed decline one line in `output` with the close standing; `grep -n MERGED_BY lib/record.sh` shows `memory_merge` untouched (`git diff origin/main -- lib/record.sh` prints no line of `memory_merge`); `bash -n lib/requests.sh lib/memory.sh` passes.

docs/architecture.md: `lib/requests.sh`'s row (the v2 branch, the order: ledger rule in node, gh's state, the review rule, the call), the guards table's *Request inbox* row with the v2 verbs' rules, the memory invariant's sentence *a merge request from the card is Michael's hand, run by `harness requests`, never `memory_merge`*; README.md's *Steering* names the card's two actions and `harness memory decline <run> --why`; journal/decisions/2026-11-10-review-surface-verbs.md gains V2-02's rows marked *default* (gh's state first; the review rule for both PRs; no `--match-head-commit`; `--comment` with the why; never `--delete-branch`; a failed decline leaves the close standing; both PRs on the card) and the rejected list (`--match-head-commit` on the card's merge, facts-only merge, `--delete-branch`, a why on merge, a second PR state for a close with a reason, a decline that fails stopping the close).

memory-requests.sh is timed once alone with `TEST_JOBS=4 bash tests/run.sh memory-requests` and its row (file, tier fast, the seconds, the reason) is added under the table in journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md; its new names are in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt, both LC_ALL=C sorted; `bash tests/run.sh memory-requests request-files` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: An Opus review of V2's whole diff against the spec's invariants 3 and 4 and A3's argv rule, its Critical and Important findings fixed test-first, simplifications applied, the docs level; the review's file is docs/plans/2026-11-10-V2-review.md.
steps: `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- lib bin tests templates docs README.md journal/decisions > /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-11-10/V2.diff`; an Opus subagent reads the diff from that file (never the conversation) and writes docs/plans/2026-11-10-V2-review.md with findings graded Critical, Important, Minor, on at least: no path lets a request merge a PR the ledger does not know or one whose review did not run (`validateRequest`'s order read, then `one()`'s branch: the ledger rule in node before any gh call, the review rule before the merge); the text and the why reach gh as argv elements only (`grep -n 'eval\|bash -c' lib/requests.sh` prints nothing); the card's merge leaves `merged_by` null (`grep -n MERGED_BY lib/record.sh lib/requests.sh` shows it set in lib/record.sh alone); a run-level declined row drops no op in `apply` and breaks neither `proposalsView` nor `latestAnswers` (the unit tests read); tests/stub-gh.sh's `pr merge <url> --merge` and `pr close <url> --comment` are gh's shapes, named to gh 2.45 in its header; the checklist's request JSON equals tests/fixtures/requests/merge.json and close-why.json but for the placeholders. A second round only when the first found something Critical.

Every Critical and Important finding is fixed with a failing check or unit test first (names into tests/fixtures/check-names.txt, and check-names-fast.txt for unit and fast names; a replaced check's old name leaves in the same commit); Minor findings are fixed or listed in the review file with why not; simplification passes the reviewer names are applied.

docs/architecture.md and README.md are read against the code as it stands (the `lib/requests.mjs` and `lib/requests.sh` rows, the *Request inbox* rows, the memory invariant, `harness memory decline <run> --why`, *Steering*) and brought level; journal/decisions/2026-11-10-review-surface-verbs.md holds every V2 default marked *default* and lists V2's replaced and removed check names each with its successor, and the milestone's count against the budget of 25 with the reason when over.

`bash -n` on every shell file the fixes touched and `node --check` on every .mjs pass; `bash tests/run.sh memory-requests request-files memory-review` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); the suite is green.
